title: Parentheses, Brackets and Braces
short: Work from the innermost grouping outward.

blocks.html: You know the order of operations. Parentheses let you change that order: whatever is inside them is worked first. When an expression needs groups inside groups, we use bigger symbols so the eye can match the pairs: parentheses $(\;)$, brackets $[\;]$ and braces $\{\;\}$.
Start with the innermost grouping symbols and work outward. Inside each pair, use the usual order: multiply and divide, then add and subtract.

A grouping symbol says “treat this as one number.” In $3 \times (8 + 2)$ you multiply 3 by the amount $8 + 2$, which is 10, so the value is 30. Without the parentheses, $3 \times 8 + 2$ is 26. Brackets and braces mean exactly the same as parentheses; they only make nested groups easier to read.

blocks.cap: The same numbers, grouped three ways. Parentheses only change the value when they change what is done first.

blocks.html: Working the outer symbols first, or dropping the inner ones. In $2 \times [5 + (6 - 2)]$, doing $2 \times 5$ first gives the wrong value. Check: find the pair of symbols with nothing grouped inside it. That pair is always first.
